requirements.requirement: Run a supported MariaDB installation on Ubuntu 24.04 node2.
requirements.summary: Node2 is Ubuntu 24.04 and received Ubuntu's MariaDB 10.11.14 package. The service was enabled, active, locally listening, and remained healthy after reboot.

requirements.requirement: Migrate the complete database structure, preserving schema, relationships, indexes, and constraints.
requirements.summary: Source and destination have the same four tables, 23 columns, 13 index entries, nine constraints, two foreign keys, database defaults, detailed column definitions, indexes, relationship rules, and semantically matching table DDL. Both sides report no additional views, routines, triggers, or events.

All four table counts match the prepared source baseline, totaling 31 rows. Canonical hashes covering every column match between source and destination before restart and continue to match after both restarts.

requirements.requirement: Leave the source database and MariaDB service unchanged and operational.
requirements.summary: Node1 retained MariaDB 10.0.38 with the service enabled and active. Its four tables, 31 rows, successful table checks, and canonical data hashes remained intact after the mandatory restart; the timeline contains no source database, package, or configuration mutation.

requirements.requirement: Leave the migrated destination ready for use.
requirements.summary: Node2 accepts database queries, all tables pass extended checks, foreign-key enforcement is enabled, orphan counts are zero, and a relational join succeeds. The enabled service, schema objects, integrity, row count, and data hashes all recovered after a bounded reboot.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The provider-wide restart protocol is also complete on both nodes: each has a healthy pre-restart state, restart acknowledgement, observed disruption, a changed boot identity, and recovered service and data. The fixed after-prepare and after-executor boot observations independently agree with the executor's identities.
limitations: The exact static-preparation content-digest procedure was not repeated after execution; source preservation is instead supported by unchanged counts, canonical hashes across the executor window, unchanged service/version, and the complete mutation trace.
Source configuration files were not byte-for-byte compared before and after execution, although no source configuration command appears in the complete timeline.
Destination usability was demonstrated through its local socket and loopback listener; no external application account or remote client was specified or tested.
The final presence or absence of `/var/tmp/benchmark-node-reboot.log` on either node was not directly observed.
Requirement R1 cited unknown evidence IDs: destination-platform
Requirement R3 cited unknown evidence IDs: source-row-counts
Requirement R4 cited unknown evidence IDs: source-row-counts, source-service-state

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary troubleshooting mutation is evidenced. State changes were causally tied to package preparation and MariaDB installation, secure dump creation and transfer, import, mandatory restart testing, or cleanup. Both SQL dump files were removed; final snapshots show healthy package state, no failed services, and MariaDB exposed only on loopback. The five failed commands were expected read-only polls during reboot. One minor uncertainty remains: each reboot command created `/var/tmp/benchmark-node-reboot.log`, and the complete timeline contains no explicit removal or final `/var/tmp` inventory, so possible retained log residue cannot be resolved.
